name: TCA9555 16-bit I/O expander
description: Texas Instruments 16-bit I2C/SMBus I/O expander: two 8-bit ports (P00-P07, P10-P17), each pin an input with a fixed internal 100 kOhm pull-up or a push-pull output (25 mA max per pin), plus an open-drain interrupt output. Runs on 1.65-5.5 V with 5 V tolerant I/O. Sold as: MusRock TCA9555 I2C I/O Expander 16-Bit GPIO Expansion Board (green 24-pin DIP-style board, 800 mil rows; J1: nINT, A1, A2, P00-P07, GND | J2: VDD, SDA, SCL, A0, P17-P10; 10k pull-ups on SDA, SCL and nINT, A0-A2 pulled low by 10k), I2C address 0x20 (0x20-0x27 via A0-A2).
eli5: Gives your board 16 extra pins to switch LEDs or read buttons, using only the two I2C wires.

buildNotes: I2C address is 0x20 + (A2 A1 A0): the board pulls A0-A2 low through 10k, so it answers at 0x20 until you tie address pins to VDD.

All pins power up as inputs (Configuration 0x06/0x07 = 0xFF) and every Output Port latch powers up at 1: write the level to Output Port 0x02/0x03 first, then clear the pin's Configuration bit to make it an output, or it starts by driving high.
Read pin levels from Input Port 0x00 (P00-P07) / 0x01 (P10-P17). Inputs have a fixed internal ~100 kOhm pull-up, so a button to GND needs no extra resistor and reads 0 when pressed.
Each pin sinks or sources at most 25 mA, each 8-pin port 100 mA sunk / 80 mA sourced, the chip 200 mA sunk / 160 mA sourced: always put a resistor in series with an LED.
The board's SDA/SCL/nINT pull-ups go to VDD: power it from 3.3 V with an ESP32 or Pico so the bus never sees 5 V (the P pins themselves are 5 V tolerant).
nINT is open-drain and goes low when an input changes; reading the Input Port clears it.
This 24-pin board has two rows 800 mil apart, so Sparkbench wires it with jumper leads to a single-row connector.

driver.code:
# TCA9555 16-bit I2C I/O expander (TI SCPS200E), MicroPython driver.
# Register map (command byte, datasheet Table 3):
#   0x00 / 0x01  Input Port 0 / 1         read-only, the levels on the pins
#   0x02 / 0x03  Output Port 0 / 1        output latches (power-up 0xFF)
#   0x04 / 0x05  Polarity Inversion 0 / 1 1 = invert that input (power-up 0x00)
#   0x06 / 0x07  Configuration 0 / 1      1 = input (power-up 0xFF), 0 = output
# Registers come in pairs: after the command byte, a 2-byte read or write
# moves from port 0 to port 1 of the same pair.
# Pins are numbered 0-15: 0-7 = P00-P07, 8-15 = P10-P17.
# Every input has a fixed internal ~100 kOhm pull-up (no register for it):
# an undriven input reads 1, a button to GND reads 0.

_INPUT0 = 0x00
_OUTPUT0 = 0x02
_POLARITY0 = 0x04
_CONFIG0 = 0x06

INPUT = 1
OUTPUT = 0


class TCA9555:
    def __init__(self, i2c, addr=0x20):
        """addr = 0x20 + A2A1A0 (0x20 with all address pins low)."""
        self.i2c = i2c
        self.addr = addr

    def _w(self, reg, val):
        self.i2c.writeto_mem(self.addr, reg, bytes([val & 0xFF]))

    def _r(self, reg):
        return self.i2c.readfrom_mem(self.addr, reg, 1)[0]

    def _bit(self, base, pin, on):
        if not 0 <= pin <= 15:
            raise ValueError('pin must be 0-15')
        reg = base + (pin >> 3)  # port 0 register, or the port 1 register right after it
        v = self._r(reg)
        v = v | (1 << (pin & 7)) if on else v & ~(1 << (pin & 7))
        self._w(reg, v)

    def pin_mode(self, pin, mode):
        """mode INPUT or OUTPUT. Set the output level with value() first:
        the latch powers up at 1, so a pin made an output drives high."""
        self._bit(_CONFIG0, pin, mode == INPUT)

    def invert(self, pin, on=True):
        """Polarity inversion of an input pin (read back as the opposite level)."""
        self._bit(_POLARITY0, pin, on)

    def value(self, pin, val=None):
        """Read a pin's level (Input Port register), or set its output latch (Output Port register)."""
        if val is None:
            if not 0 <= pin <= 15:
                raise ValueError('pin must be 0-15')
            return (self._r(_INPUT0 + (pin >> 3)) >> (pin & 7)) & 1
        self._bit(_OUTPUT0, pin, val)

    def read_port(self):
        """All 16 pin levels: bits 0-7 = P00-P07, bits 8-15 = P10-P17."""
        d = self.i2c.readfrom_mem(self.addr, _INPUT0, 2)  # Input Port 0 then Input Port 1
        return d[0] | (d[1] << 8)

    def write_port(self, val):
        """Set all 16 output latches: bits 0-7 = P00-P07, bits 8-15 = P10-P17."""
        self.i2c.writeto_mem(self.addr, _OUTPUT0, bytes([val & 0xFF, (val >> 8) & 0xFF]))

    def config_port(self, inputs):
        """16-bit direction mask in one go (1 = input, 0 = output)."""
        self.i2c.writeto_mem(self.addr, _CONFIG0, bytes([inputs & 0xFF, (inputs >> 8) & 0xFF]))

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from tca9555 import TCA9555, INPUT, OUTPUT

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}))
io = TCA9555(i2c)          # address 0x20 (A0-A2 pulled low on the board)
io.value(0, 0)             # latch P00 low first (it powers up at 1)...
io.pin_mode(0, OUTPUT)     # ...then make P00 an output for an LED (through a resistor)
io.pin_mode(8, INPUT)      # P10 reads a button wired to GND (internal pull-up)
while True:
    pressed = 1 if io.value(8) == 0 else 0
    io.value(0, pressed)   # LED on while the button is held
    print('BTN=%d LED=%d' % (pressed, pressed))
    time.sleep_ms(200)
